comparison.objective: Candidate commissions and locks a robot-axis shock absorber through iterative dynamic tuning; pr-727 removes a strong magnet from a steel plate and places it at least 5 cm away without reattachment.
comparison.physical_skill: Candidate requires recessed hex-key insertion, setscrew loosening/torque-limited relocking, fine collar rotation, counterholding, and repeated physical cycling. pr-727 requires bimanual plate restraint, tangential magnet sliding by a knob, controlled separation, placement, and release. Bimanual stabilization is shared only as a generic primitive.
comparison.success_condition: Candidate requires two repeatable ≥0.85 J impacts within the stated velocity range, ≤12 mm travel, no hard-stop strike/overload/excess rebound, and bounded post-lock collar drift, with safety and anti-state-write constraints. pr-727 requires holding the plate, setting the magnet down ≥5 cm away, releasing it, and preventing snap-back. Its indexed record has no spec versions and does not define numeric plate-retention or snap-back thresholds beyond the 5 cm placement distance.
comparison.reason: The tested abilities are meaningfully different: tool-mediated adjustment and retention followed by dynamic damper validation versus force-controlled magnetic separation and safe placement. Different geometry is not the basis of the verdict, and the shared generic bimanual element does not establish overlap.
